description: SOC-thermal Nernst + Arrhenius-R model for hydrogen-bromine flow battery stack. Positive: Br2/Br- redox; negative: H+/H2. Temperature range 20-60 degC.

unit.name: Generic 30-cell H2-Br2 flow battery stack, 200 cm2 electrode area
unit.source: Livshits, V. et al. (2006). J. Power Sources 160, 1298; Cho, K. T. et al. (2012). J. Electrochem. Soc. 159, A1806; Tucker, M. C. et al. (2015). J. Electrochem. Soc. 162, A2159

E0.note: Standard cell potential Br2/Br- vs H+/H2: 1.065-1.09 V. Using 1.09 V at 25 degC.

R_cell_ohm_cm2_ref.note: Area-specific resistance at T_ref; HBrFB has fast H2/H+ kinetics (Pt/C), resistance dominated by membrane (Nafion) ~ 2-3 Ohm.cm2

electrolyte_conc_M.note: HBr electrolyte concentration; Br2 concentration 0.1-1 M

pump_loss_coefficient.note: Pump parasitic for electrolyte side; H2 side pump is also included in this coefficient

E_a.note: Activation energy for HBrFB cell resistance; Nafion membrane proton conductivity E_a ~ 10-20 kJ/mol; using representative 14 kJ/mol.
E_a.source: Cho et al. (2012) J. Electrochem. Soc. 159, A1806; Tucker et al. (2015) J. Electrochem. Soc. 162, A2159

dOCV_dT.note: Temperature coefficient of standard potential for Br2/Br- vs H2/H+. dE0/dT = -delta_S/(n*F). For Br2(aq)+H2(g)->2HBr(aq): delta_S ~ -97 J/mol/K -> dE0/dT = 97/(2*96485) ~ 0.00050 V/K. Experimental values: -0.4 to -0.6 mV/K cell, using -0.50 mV/K.
dOCV_dT.source: Livshits et al. (2006) J. Power Sources 160, 1298; Atkins Physical Chemistry (2014) thermodynamic data for HBr(aq) formation

T_min.note: 20 degC lower limit (Br2 vapor pressure and dissolution constraints)

T_max.note: 60 degC upper limit (membrane degradation, Br2 volatility above 60 degC)

current.note: positive=discharge; HBrFB supports high current density due to fast H2 kinetics
